# Module `asyncs`

async - a multi-threaded executor with stackful-fiber tasks.

This is the real executor that the earlier `tasks` module's fire-and-forget
threads were steps toward. Each async_spawn task runs on its own stack (a
fiber) pinned to one of the pool's worker threads (one scheduler per CPU core),
and a running fiber can suspend cooperatively without blocking its worker:

  import asyncs
  a<Int> = async_spawn(|| -> { async_sleep_ms(40); return 10 }) else 0
  b<Int> = async_spawn(|| -> { async_sleep_ms(5); return 32 }) else 0
  v1 = async_await(a)   // drives the loop until a completes -> 10
  v2 = async_await(b)   // -> 32   (took ~40ms total, not ~45ms)

Suspension points are the suspendable intrinsics: async_yield() (round-robin
fairness), async_sleep_ms(ms) (a timer, not a thread sleep, so other tasks
proceed), and async_await(t) (block until task `t` completes, returning it).
Because the fibers are stackful, a fn() can suspend mid-body simply by calling
these -- no state-machine transform is required.

Lifecycle: tasks stay valid across main-thread awaits, so you can spawn
several and await them in any order. async_detach(t) reclaims a single
completed task early (call after polling/awaiting; the handle must not be used
afterwards), so a long-lived program can recycle fibers instead of one per
spawn. async_run_all() runs whatever is left and then reclaims every task; a
leftover-task atexit hook stops the worker pool and reclaims anything forgotten.

Fallible operations follow the engine-wide `T?` shape (PROGRAMMERS_GUIDE
§3.16): async_spawn and async_accept return `Int?` and are absent on failure
(no more `0`/`-1` sentinels); async_poll is a native `Int?` -- absent while the
fiber is still running, present holding its result (which may legitimately be
-1). async_connect returns `Bool?` (present on success), async_send `Int?`
(bytes written), async_recv `String?` (lossless; absent on error/EOF), and
async_sleep_ms `Bool?` (always present). async_await stays a plain Int: on a
valid handle it always blocks until a result arrives, so it has no absence to
report. async_detach keeps its documented status code (0 ok / -1 already
detached / -3 waiter attached) rather than collapsing those distinct outcomes
to a presence bit; the async I/O failure diagnostics live in
network::socket_error_code()/socket_error_message().

<a id="sym-async_accept"></a>
### `async_accept` · fn

```
async_accept(fd<Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Accept a pending connection on a listening socket, suspending until one
arrives. Returns `Int?` -- present holding the connected descriptor (>= 0) on
success, absent on failure. The failure diagnostic lives in
network::socket_error_code()/socket_error_message().

<a id="sym-async_await"></a>
### `async_await` · fn

```
async_await(t<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Block until task `t` completes and return its closure result. On a valid handle
the result is always delivered (it may be any Int, including -1); only an
invalid handle yields -1. From the entry thread this parks until the worker
delivers it; from inside a fiber it suspends that fiber while the pool
continues other work.

<a id="sym-async_connect"></a>
### `async_connect` · fn

```
async_connect(fd<Int>, ip<String>, port<Int>)<Bool?> ->
```

Non-blocking connect, suspending until established or refused. Returns `Bool?`
-- present on success, absent on failure (see
network::socket_error_code()/socket_error_message()).

<a id="sym-async_detach"></a>
### `async_detach` · fn

```
async_detach(t<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Reclaim a completed task, freeing its fiber stack and captured environment so
long-lived programs don't accumulate one fiber per spawn. The task must no
longer be awaited; the handle must not be used afterwards. If the fiber is
already finished the task is freed immediately; a still-running task is marked
and reclaimed by its worker as soon as it completes, so a slow fetch still
self-reaps. Returns a status code (not a presence bit) so callers can
distinguish the outcomes: 0 on success, -1 if already detached, -3 if a waiter
is still attached, -2 on an invalid handle.

<a id="sym-async_poll"></a>
### `async_poll` · fn

```
async_poll(t<Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Non-blocking presence check: returns `Int?` -- present holding the task's
result once the fiber has finished (the result may legitimately be -1), absent
while it is still running. Unwrap with `else default` or `match`.

<a id="sym-async_recv"></a>
### `async_recv` · fn

```
async_recv(fd<Int>, maxlen<Int>)<String?> ->
```

Receive up to `maxlen` bytes from `fd`, suspending until data is readable.
Returns a lossless `String?` -- present holding the bytes read (which may
legitimately be empty), absent on error/EOF, so an empty read is never
conflated with a failed read.

<a id="sym-async_run_all"></a>
### `async_run_all` · fn

```
async_run_all()<Int> ->
```

Run the pool until no queued work or pending timer remain, then reclaim tasks.

<a id="sym-async_send"></a>
### `async_send` · fn

```
async_send(fd<Int>, data<String>)<Int?> ->
```

Send all of `data` on `fd`, suspending until the socket accepts it. Returns
`Int?` -- present holding the number of bytes sent, absent on failure.

<a id="sym-async_sleep_ms"></a>
### `async_sleep_ms` · fn

```
async_sleep_ms(ms<Int>)<Bool?> ->
```

Cooperative sleep: suspend the current fiber for `ms` on a timer so other loop
work proceeds. Outside a fiber this sleeps the calling thread. Returns `Bool?`
-- always present (a sleep cannot fail).

<a id="sym-async_spawn"></a>
### `async_spawn` · fn

```
async_spawn(work<fn() -> Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Enqueue `work` (a fn() -> Int) on the worker pool. Returns `Int?` -- present
holding the task handle (>= 1) on success, absent when pool setup fails. The
pool runs on the next async_await/async_run_all.

<a id="sym-async_yield"></a>
### `async_yield` · fn

```
async_yield()<Int> ->
```

Cooperative yield: suspend the current fiber and reschedule it (a no-op if
called outside a fiber).
